original_value: Blossom is an open-source social robotics platform responding to three challenges in human-robot interaction (HRI) research: (1) Designing, manufacturing, and programming social robots requires a high level of technical knowledge; (2) social robot designs are fixed in appearance and movement capabilities, making them hard to adapt to a specific application; and (3) the use of rigid mechanisms and hard outer shells limits the robots’ expressive capabilities. Addressing these challenges, Blossom aims at three design objectives: accessibility, flexibility, and expressiveness. The robot’s mechanism can be quickly assembled and partially extended by end-users. Blossom’s appearance is open-ended through handcrafted fabric exteriors created and customized by users. Smooth organic movements are achieved with tensile mechanisms, elastic components, and a soft exterior cover attached loosely to the body. Blossom’s smartphone-based gesture generation requires neither programming nor character animation experience, allowing lay users to create their own behaviors. All elements in the design were conceived with a low barrier-of-entry in mind. The result is an accessible and customizable social robot for researchers. This article details the implementation of Blossom’s design and demonstrates the platform’s potential through four field deployment case studies.

result.paraphrase: Blossom is an open-source platform for social robotics that addresses three challenges in HRI research: designing, building, and programming social robots demands substantial technical expertise; social robot designs are typically locked in their appearance and motion capabilities, which makes them difficult to adapt for a particular use case; and rigid mechanisms with hard outer shells restrict expressive ability. To meet these challenges, Blossom pursues three design goals: accessibility, flexibility, and expressiveness. Its mechanism can be assembled quickly and partially extended by end users. Blossom’s look is open-ended thanks to handcrafted fabric exteriors that users create and customize. Smooth, organic motion is enabled by tensile mechanisms, elastic components, and a soft outer cover loosely attached to the body. Its smartphone-based gesture generation needs no programming or character-animation experience, enabling lay users to produce their own behaviors. Every part of the design was developed with a low barrier to entry in mind. The result is an accessible, customizable social robot for researchers. This article presents Blossom’s implementation and illustrates the platform’s potential through four field deployment case studies.
